## Summary

`/status` keeps reporting `Agents.md: <none>` for the rest of a session after `/init` creates an `AGENTS.md`, on any platform.

## Reproduction

1. Start a session in a directory with no `AGENTS.md`.
2. Run `/init` and let it write `AGENTS.md`.
3. Run `/status`.

Expected: the new file is discovered. Actual: `Agents.md: <none>`, and it stays that way until a new session is started.

Add a user-configurable policy for automatically reloading `AGENTS.md` instructions, with an explicit **freeze** option. This is a token-efficiency and session-consistency preference, useful even when the entire conversation fits comfortably within the context window.

Related bug: #43295 tracks automatic instruction reload overflowing the context window and locking a previously usable session. **That failure needs to be handled independently of this feature request.** This enhanceme

items.snippet:
The problem
My AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files kept growing, but I had no safe way to tell which instructions were still useful and which were stale, duplicated, or too broad.
So I built Skill Sunset, a local, read-only audit for agent instruction files. The important constraint is: TEST is not RETIRE. A suspicious rule is not removed just because a heuristic dislikes it.
npx skill-sunset@latest audit --codex --open
It scans AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and generic SKILL.md files, then produces an eviden
items.title: Skill Sunset: a local, read-only audit for stale AGENTS.md rules

items.snippet:
Instructions files are advice. The agent reads them, agrees, and then writes the thing you told it not to — a hardcoded connection string, a duplicate route handler, await on a synchronous call.
Sarge makes the rules enforceable instead of advisory. Every file the agent writes gets judged against a rule book in the repo — by a local model, not a regex — and the run refuses while a rule is broken. The agent gets the failure back and fixes it. Break the same rule twice and a tutor writes the corre
items.title: Sarge: a rule check that refuses the run, instead of another line in the instructions file

I run a few projects with Codex and Claude Code, and the part that wore me out was not the coding. So I built the operations layer and open-sourced it.
Agent 007 (https://github.com/bill10/agent-007) is a small web app, one command (npx @bill10/agent-007), that:

starts Codex (or Claude Code, or any CLI agent) in web terminals, each i
items.title: Agent 007: a job board and a manager agent for Codex (and Claude Code) workers, in your browser
